Reports: headers, footers, titles, footnotes and tokens

Source: vignettes/articles/reports.Rmd
reports.Rmd

The report spec is the document around a table, a listing or a figure: the page, the running header and footer, the titles and footnotes, a watermark. tfl_report_code() writes the rtfreporter calls it stands for (doc <- rtf_document(...), rtf_section(), rtf_tables(), rtf_titles(), rtf_footnotes()), and tfl_report() makes the same document from a plan or pages in hand.

library(tflspec)
library(rtfreporter)

The sheets

Sheet One row per Holds
report report type (table, listing, figure, user), file ({output_id}.rtf), program, font sizes, page_header / page_footer, watermark, a figure’s size
page report paper, orientation, margins, the document’s text defaults; font and font_size_half_points (the study’s row is the company’s)
header, footer, titles, footnotes line line, left, center, right
tokens token name, value: a token of one’s own, {STUDY} in any cell above

plus the study keys output_path (where the RTF files go) and program_dir (where the programs are, for {PROGRAM}).

Written once for the study

The output_id rule makes the study’s look a matter of default rows (a blank output_id), written once; each report adds or replaces only what is its own. On the line sheets the line number is the key:

  • the study’s page header is default lines 1 and 2, and each report’s titles follow on its own lines 3, 4, …;
  • a run line 99 in the default footer closes every report;
  • a report’s line replaces the default line of the same number, and a report’s line that says (none) takes it out.
df <- function(...) data.frame(..., stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

spec <- tfl_table_spec(
  study = c(output_path = "output", program_dir = "programs"),
  report = df(output_id = c(NA, "T-14-1-1", "T-14-3-1"),
              file = c("{output_id}.rtf", NA, NA),
              watermark = c("DRAFT", NA, NA)),
  header = df(output_id = c(NA, NA, "T-14-1-1", "T-14-1-1", "T-14-3-1"),
              line = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 3),
              left = c("{SPONSOR}", "Protocol: {STUDY}", NA, NA, NA),
              center = c(NA, NA, "Table 14.1.1", "Demographics",
                         "Table 14.3.1"),
              right = c("{CUTOFF}", "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}",
                        NA, NA, NA)),
  footer = df(output_id = c(NA, "T-14-3-1"), line = c(99, 99),
              left = c("{PROGRAM}   Generated on: {DATETIME}", "(none)")),
  footnotes = df(output_id = "T-14-3-1", line = 1,
                 left = "MedDRA version {MEDDRA}."),
  tokens = df(output_id = c(NA, NA, NA, NA, "T-14-3-1"),
              name = c("SPONSOR", "STUDY", "CUTOFF", "MEDDRA", "CUTOFF"),
              value = c("ACME Pharma", "ABC-123", "Data cut-off: 01JUN2026",
                        "27.1", "Data cut-off: 01SEP2026")))

The demographics table gets the study’s header with its own two title lines, the study’s run line, and the study’s tokens:

cat(tfl_report_code(spec, "T-14-1-1", content = "plan"), sep = "\n")
doc <- rtf_document(
  watermark = "DRAFT",
  program_fallback = "programs/T-14-1-1",
  tokens = list(
    SPONSOR = "ACME Pharma",
    STUDY = "ABC-123",
    CUTOFF = "Data cut-off: 01JUN2026",
    MEDDRA = "27.1"
  ),
  file = "output/T-14-1-1.rtf"
) |>
  rtf_section(
    header = rtf_header(
      list(
        c(l = "{SPONSOR}", r = "{CUTOFF}"),
        c(l = "Protocol: {STUDY}", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"),
        c(c = "Table 14.1.1"),
        c(c = "Demographics")
      )
    ),
    footer = rtf_footer(list(c(l = "{PROGRAM}   Generated on: {DATETIME}")))
  ) |>
  rtf_tables(plan)

The AE table has its own cut-off (its CUTOFF row replaces the study’s), a footnote, and no run line (its line 99 says (none)):

cat(tfl_report_code(spec, "T-14-3-1", content = "plan"), sep = "\n")
doc <- rtf_document(
  watermark = "DRAFT",
  program_fallback = "programs/T-14-3-1",
  tokens = list(
    SPONSOR = "ACME Pharma",
    STUDY = "ABC-123",
    MEDDRA = "27.1",
    CUTOFF = "Data cut-off: 01SEP2026"
  ),
  file = "output/T-14-3-1.rtf"
) |>
  rtf_section(
    header = rtf_header(
      list(
        c(l = "{SPONSOR}", r = "{CUTOFF}"),
        c(l = "Protocol: {STUDY}", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"),
        c(c = "Table 14.3.1")
      )
    )
  ) |>
  rtf_tables(plan) |>
  rtf_footnotes(list(list(c(l = "MedDRA version {MEDDRA}."))))

Tokens

A cell of the header, footer, titles or footnotes may say a token:

  • rtfreporter’s own, filled when the file is written: {PAGE}, {TOTAL_PAGES}, {PROGRAM} (or {PROGRAM_FULL}, its absolute path) and {DATETIME}. {PROGRAM} is the report sheet’s program joined to program_dir; with program blank, it is the file name of the program that runs (and the report’s id only when none is found).
  • one’s own, from the tokens sheet: a name in upper case (a letter, then letters, digits or _), not one of rtfreporter’s. A blank output_id is the study’s default; a report’s row of the same name replaces it, and (none) takes it out. They go to rtf_document(tokens = ).

A value that is the same for every report – the sponsor, the protocol, the cut-off – is written once, as a study row of the tokens sheet; the header and footer say {SPONSOR} and never repeat it.

Each report’s own tokens

A report’s header, footer, titles and footnotes may also say its own tokens, so that one header serves every report:

  • {OUTPUT_ID} – the report’s id;
  • {OUTPUT_LABEL} – made from the id: “T-14-1-1” is “Table 14.1.1” (the kind from the first letter, the number from the first digit, separators made dots); tokens rows OUTPUT_KIND_TABLE / _LISTING / _FIGURE give other words;
  • {OUTPUT_TITLE}, {OUTPUT_POPULATION}, {OUTPUT_SECTION}, {STUDY_ID} – blank unless the tokens sheet gives them (tflplanner writes them from a TOC).

A band line left with nothing but empty tokens (and brackets: <{OUTPUT_POPULATION}>) is not printed. tfl_report_tokens() shows the values a report fills them with:

sp <- tfl_table_spec(
  report = df(output_id = c("T-14-1-1", "T-14-3-1"), type = "table"),
  page = df(output_id = c(NA, "T-14-3-1"), font = c("Courier New", NA),
            font_size_half_points = c("18", "16")),
  header = df(output_id = NA, line = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
              left = c("{COMPANY}", "PROTOCOL: {STUDY_ID}", NA, NA, NA),
              center = c(NA, NA, "{OUTPUT_LABEL}", "{OUTPUT_TITLE}",
                         "<{OUTPUT_POPULATION}>"),
              right = c(NA, "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}", NA, NA, NA)),
  tokens = df(output_id = c(NA, NA, "T-14-1-1", "T-14-1-1", "T-14-3-1"),
              name = c("COMPANY", "STUDY_ID", "OUTPUT_TITLE",
                       "OUTPUT_POPULATION", "OUTPUT_TITLE"),
              value = c("Sample Pharma", "ABC-123",
                        "Demographic Characteristics", "Safety Analysis Set",
                        "Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events")))
tfl_report_tokens(sp, "T-14-1-1")
#>                       COMPANY                  OUTPUT_LABEL 
#>               "Sample Pharma"                "Table 14.1.1" 
#>                  OUTPUT_TITLE             OUTPUT_POPULATION 
#> "Demographic Characteristics"         "Safety Analysis Set" 
#>                      STUDY_ID 
#>                     "ABC-123"

The company’s font, and the study’s setup written once

The page sheet’s font and font_size_half_points set the document’s font. The study’s row (a blank output_id) is the company’s; a report’s row that says its own wins (the AE table above is a size smaller). Blank: rtfreporter’s own (Courier, 9 pt).

What every report shares – that font, the study’s tokens, the running header and footer – tfl_report_setup_code() writes once, as the code a study’s report programs source:

cat(tfl_report_setup_code(sp), sep = "\n")
options(
  rtfreporter.font = "Courier New",
  rtfreporter.font_size_half_points = 18
)
options(
  rtfreporter.tokens = list(COMPANY = "Sample Pharma", STUDY_ID = "ABC-123")
)
study_header_lines <- list(
  c(l = "{COMPANY}"),
  c(l = "PROTOCOL: {STUDY_ID}", r = "Page {PAGE} of {TOTAL_PAGES}"),
  c(c = "{OUTPUT_LABEL}"),
  c(c = "{OUTPUT_TITLE}"),
  c(c = "<{OUTPUT_POPULATION}>")
)
study_header <- rtf_header(study_header_lines, drop_empty_rows = TRUE)

A report’s program written with tfl_report_code(setup = TRUE) then says only what is its own – its tokens, a font of its own – and the study’s values are in one place, in the definition and in the code:

cat(tfl_report_code(sp, "T-14-3-1", content = "plan", setup = TRUE), sep = "\n")
doc <- rtf_document(
  default_format = rtf_default_format(font_size_half_points = 16),
  program_fallback = "T-14-3-1",
  tokens = list(
    OUTPUT_LABEL = "Table 14.3.1",
    OUTPUT_TITLE = "Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events",
    OUTPUT_POPULATION = ""
  ),
  file = "T-14-3-1.rtf"
) |>
  rtf_section(header = study_header) |>
  rtf_tables(plan)

A program standing alone (setup = FALSE, the default) says them itself; the file is the same either way.

Page patterns

Some reports want a page that differs from the study’s: a compact landscape page, another footer. The report sheets (report, page, header, footer, titles, footnotes, tokens) hold named page patterns besides the blank rows: rows whose output_id is @ and a name (@Compact), saying only what differs from Standard (the blank rows). A report chooses one in report$pattern (blank: Standard). Its own rows win over its pattern’s, and the pattern’s over Standard’s, by each sheet’s usual rules; (none) takes a line out at either level. What a pattern changes is written in its reports’ programs; Standard stays in the study’s setup.

The document

tfl_report() makes the document from the content – a plan, rtftable pages, or a plain data frame as here; tfl_report_path() says where it goes (output_path and the report’s file):

content <- data.frame(Statistic = "n", `Drug X` = "80", Control = "78", check.names = FALSE)
doc <- tfl_report(spec, "T-14-1-1", content = content)
tfl_report_path(spec, "T-14-1-1")
#> [1] "output/T-14-1-1.rtf"
generate_rtfreport(doc, tfl_report_path(spec, "T-14-1-1"), overwrite = TRUE)

The example workbook

report.xlsx in the package is a study’s report spec for the five example tables: the sponsor and protocol on lines 1 and 2 of the default header, each table’s titles on its lines 3 to 6, a run line 99 in the default footer, and a PK table that puts its run line under the table instead (page_footer = FALSE).

ex <- system.file("extdata", "ard-spec", package = "tflspec")
rs <- tfl_read_report_spec(file.path(ex, c("report.xlsx", "study.xlsx")))
rs$report[, c("output_id", "type", "file", "page_footer", "note")]
#>   output_id  type            file page_footer                              note
#> 1      <NA> table {output_id}.rtf        <NA>              the study's defaults
#> 2        LB  <NA>            <NA>        <NA>         one section per parameter
#> 3        PK  <NA>            <NA>       FALSE the run line goes under the table

A company’s TOC as report specs

A study’s list of outputs usually exists before any table, in the company’s own workbook. tfl_read_toc() reads it through a map of its columns, and gives the report, titles and footnotes sheets – every report exists, titled, before a table is written:

toc <- file.path(tempdir(), "toc.csv")
write.csv(df(
  `Output No.` = c("", "T-14-1-1", "T-14-3-1", "L-16-2-7"),
  Title = c("14.1 Demographics", "Demographic Characteristics",
            "Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events", "Listing of Serious AEs"),
  `Analysis Set` = c("", "Safety Analysis Set", "Safety Analysis Set",
                     "Safety Analysis Set"),
  Datasets = c("", "ADSL", "ADSL, ADAE", "ADAE"),
  check.names = FALSE), toc, row.names = FALSE)

sp <- tfl_read_toc(toc, map = list(output_id = "Output No.", title = "Title",
                                   population = "Analysis Set",
                                   datasets = "Datasets"))
sp$report[, c("output_id", "type")]
#>   output_id    type
#> 1  T-14-1-1   table
#> 2  T-14-3-1   table
#> 3  L-16-2-7 listing
sp$titles[, c("output_id", "line", "center")]
#>   output_id line                            center
#> 1  T-14-1-1    1       Demographic Characteristics
#> 2  T-14-1-1    2               Safety Analysis Set
#> 3  T-14-3-1    1 Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events
#> 4  T-14-3-1    2               Safety Analysis Set
#> 5  L-16-2-7    1            Listing of Serious AEs
#> 6  L-16-2-7    2               Safety Analysis Set
attr(sp, "sections")
#>            T-14-1-1            T-14-3-1            L-16-2-7 
#> "14.1 Demographics" "14.1 Demographics" "14.1 Demographics"
attr(sp, "datasets")
#>      T-14-1-1      T-14-3-1      L-16-2-7 
#>        "ADSL" "ADSL | ADAE"        "ADAE"

The kind of each report comes from its id (T-, L-, F-) when the TOC does not say it; a heading row (“14.1 Demographics”) is each report’s section. Write the result with tfl_write_specs("spec/report.xlsx", report = sp) (or tfl_write_report_spec()), and open it in Excel or in tflplanner.
